title: San Diego view
summary: The research desk: findings inbox, drafts, subject dossier, research, and the case workbench.

paragraphs: The default view. From top to bottom it holds the post-ingest brief, the subject dossier, Needs attention, the watchlist and standing searches, autonomous research, and a panel that opens the case workbench.

sections.heading: Parts
items: Post-ingest brief (headed Just landed): a non-modal panel that opens after a sync stops and lists findings discovered in the last 15 minutes. It appears only on this view.

Needs attention: one ranked list of new findings, agencies with counted statutory violations, the next meeting within two weeks, and watch changes. The window control beside the title sets how far back "new" reaches: since you last opened the app, the last day, week or month, or any time. A source that did not load is named under the list rather than leaving it silently shorter.
All findings are in the Story desk view, under All findings. See Findings inbox.
Cross-corpus explorer (in a drawer): shared language, temporal shifts, orphan topics and reused grounds across agencies, with a jurisdiction by detector heat map.
Collapsed drawers: cross-corpus patterns; topics; plan an investigation or draft a request manually; collection, coverage and storage; browse sources and add records.
Show response analytics: request counts, closure and deadline rates, and outlier charts. See Response analytics.

sections.heading: Response analytics
paragraphs: Charts here describe outliers relative to other agencies (a z-score at or above 2 is called a critical outlier). An outlier is a statistical statement about being slower than peers. It is not a legal finding. A panel whose query failed says so instead of showing zero.

title: Patterns view
summary: Corpus-wide connections backed by source excerpts, and the entity graph.

paragraphs: Patterns lists connections found across everything you ingested: exact and near copies, shared authorities, shared entities, recurring language, date clusters, and entity relationships. Each signal opens an evidence chain of source excerpts with the document hash.

sections.heading: Controls
items: Minimum evidence, Confidence, Indexed after/before, and Required terms narrow the list. Preview results runs the query.
Recipes save the exact controls in this browser profile on this Mac. They never change source evidence.
The pattern type buttons filter by signal kind.

sections.heading: Entity graph
paragraphs: Pick one of the most-cited entities to centre the graph. Dotted arcs with a hollow marker are co-occurrence: proximity this app computed, not a relationship any document stated. Labelled arcs with a solid diamond are relations read from the text (signed by, approved, cites, promises, delivered, supersedes, amends). Line thickness reads shared documents. Node shape shows the validation grade: check digit passed, format validated, gazetteer hit, or pattern only, which is a lead. Trace finds a path of up to four hops between two entity ids.

Above the drawing, three toggles show relationships by how they are known: stated in text, derived by this app, or asserted by a source. As of shows relationships whose recorded dates include that day. A relationship with no recorded dates is not assumed valid on any date, so it is hidden unless Include undated is checked. Filtered relationships are hidden, not absent, and the count says how many are shown.

When a neighbouring entity has a name that looks like another spelling of the centre, such as a different capitalisation, punctuation or company suffix, the panel lists it as a possible duplicate. Combine in this view reads that entity's relationships and shows them together with the centre's. Shared-document counts keep the larger of the two rather than adding them, because one document can mention both spellings. Split undoes it. A similar name is a lead, not proof of identity, and a combined view is not saved: it applies to this session only.

sections.heading: When the index is empty or fails
paragraphs: An empty graph says nothing has been indexed. A failed read says the index did not answer, which is not a statement that no relationships exist. A rebuild discards entity identifiers, so an old selection can go stale.

title: Analysis view
summary: Local semantic search and read-only SQL over imported tables.

paragraphs: Analysis works on the text and tables already on your Mac. Panels appear in this order.

sections.heading: Panels
items: What stands out: leads worth raising, each with an Evidence and method line (snapshot id and SHA-256) and an Explore this finding button that opens its query. For a table of service reports (a service type, a close date, and an opened date or recorded age, as in Get It Done) the checks count reports open more than a year by service, areas whose open reports are older or whose reports closed slower than the median across all areas, places named by ten or more open reports, and reports referred elsewhere with no outcome recorded. An area listed as slower in three or more imported tables is reported as recurring. When the same source was imported on two dates, the reports that left the open file and the new ones that arrived are counted by service, with what the imported tables record of those that left: a close date, a referral, or no record. Where a published table would answer what the imported ones cannot (a newer copy of the Get It Done open file after seven days, or the closed-reports year for reports that left), a Missing data line names it; it is fetched automatically when Data upkeep has Recheck sources on, or with Fetch it now. These are counts of the publisher’s records, not findings of fault: an open report does not prove the problem persists, and a difference between areas can reflect what was reported. Notes about a table itself (coverage, gaps, record shares) are folded beneath the leads. Failed checks retry after a delay.
Semantic Index: Initialize model, Index missing, Rebuild and Cancel. The first initialization downloads the embedding model files (see Data handling). Until it is ready, search is exact-word only.

Analytical Import: turn an acquired table or a local CSV, TSV, JSON, GeoJSON, JSONL, XLSX, XLS or ODS file into a queryable table. Tick Partial export if completeness is not established. Fetch and import downloads a published City or SANDAG table by name: SDPD NIBRS offenses, SDPD calls for service or Get It Done encampment reports for a year, Get It Done open reports for all services as published today, SANDAG schools, or SANDAG transit stops. A Get It Done closed-year file is kept either for the Encampment service or, as Get It Done closed reports (those seen open), for the reports already present in an imported open copy; the snapshot records the publisher file’s SHA-256 beside the subset’s.
Data discovery: compare a measure over groups and periods. Confirm units and row meaning before interpreting a total.

Encampment ordinance observations: Measure counts SDMC 63.0404 activity from imported tables. From an SDPD arrests and citations log (activityNumber, activityDate, violationSection): how many fall between 9:00 p.m. and 5:30 a.m., the 63.0405(b) window for 63.0404(a) citations, with activities exactly at either endpoint listed apart. From NIBRS offenses: distance to the nearest school and transit station, in bands of 1,320 and 2,640 feet that stand in for “two blocks”. These are observations, not findings of a violation; shelter availability, posted signs and park designations are listed under Not measured.
Hybrid retrieval: search extracted text. Exact search needs every word. A missing match does not show the sources lack the information.
Budget versus actuals: sums each side by year, fund, funds center and account, keeps missing counterparts visible, and does not reconcile transfers or show program effectiveness.
SQL Analysis: one read-only SELECT at a time. Run shows up to 500 rows and Export CSV up to 10,000. Datasets marked Partial / unverified coverage were imported with completeness not established.
Schema Browser lists tables and columns.

title: Evidence view
summary: Search requests, read their documents, and save leads to the briefing.

sections.heading: Timeline
paragraphs: Switch Records to Timeline, or run Show evidence timeline from the command palette, for one dated list drawn from your tracked requests, detector findings, watch changes and case records. Each row says what its date means. Event date is when something happened, as you recorded it. Last seen is when a detector last observed a finding, and Noticed by this app is when a watch check saw a change. Those two can be later than the event. Due or modeled date is a deadline you recorded or one the statutory clock computed from your filing date, not something observed. Case rows name the citations they rest on and the rung each was verified at, or say that no citation is recorded. The Lane menu narrows the list to one request's statutory clock or to the events a question's hypothesis cites, so competing hypotheses can be read side by side. When two recorded sources give the same subject different dates, both are listed above the timeline and neither is chosen. Show basis reveals the quoted sentence or explanation behind a row. Inspect in evidence opens the finding's records.

Filter by source, date range or text. If a source cannot be read, the timeline names it as missing instead of showing the rest as complete. Only the most recent 500 findings and 200 watch changes are loaded, and the page says when that limit applies. A row whose date cannot be read is counted and left out, never placed at a guessed date.

sections.heading: Searching
paragraphs: The search box looks in request metadata and extracted text. Every word must occur; words in double quotes must occur together, in order, within one request field or one document. Qualifiers agency:, portal:, status: and flag: narrow results. Plain-language mode turns a sentence into those filters. Results are capped at 500, and a count of 500+ means more may exist. If a search fails, the last successful results stay on screen with a banner saying so.

Each result says where your text is visible: in the title, in the description, or not shown here. Not shown means the match may be in the full description or in a document's extracted text. It does not mean the text is absent. An empty result lists what was searched and offers to remove each filter that narrowed it. It does not show that no such record exists.

Watch this text for changes saves the words as a watch that is checked after each ingest. It covers all sources and ignores the department, status and policy filters. Copy search record puts a query ID, the text, filters, source count, result count and a corpus-state digest on the clipboard, with the time of the search. The ID names the query, not its answer. The digest covers extracted document text only, so the same query against the same digest returns the same document-text matches, while request status and titles can still change.

sections.heading: Reading a request
items: Select a record for its case context: dates, status, description and the Legal compliance panel.
Save lead to briefing stores it locally for the Briefing view.
Public documents lists files with their extraction state. Only searchable or recovered documents open. Personal information is masked in what you read.
Copy evidence link, in the document viewer, copies a portal, request, document and character offset so you can return to the same passage.

sections.heading: Deadline appeal draft
paragraphs: Requests carrying a statutory latency flag show appeal actions. Drafts and saved files stay on this Mac. The app does not send anything. See Request and appeal drafts.

title: Activity view
summary: Ingestion queues, throughput and errors for this session.

paragraphs: Activity is a control room for ingestion. Nothing on it is persisted: the event stream and counters reset when you quit the app.

items: Session throughput: requests processed, tasks completed, documents saved, and task exceptions.
Event stream: filter by text or show errors only, Export JSON, or clear the session telemetry.
Source runtimes: running or stopped, done, active and queued counts per source.
Extraction event stream: the same feed inside the Evidence view.
The sidebar footer shows worker capacity out of five and whether local OCR handles images and PDFs, images only, or is unavailable. Hover it for the probe details.

sections.heading: Local OCR
paragraphs: On a Mac, OCR uses the text recognition built into macOS (Apple Vision), and scanned PDFs are rendered page by page with PDFKit at up to 300 DPI. Nothing needs to be installed. On other systems the app runs Tesseract with its eng language pack for images and Poppler's pdftoppm for scanned PDFs, which must be installed from the system's package manager; until both are, a scanned document whose text cannot be read is kept but its text is not searchable. Either way OCR runs on this computer and sends nothing anywhere.
When a query behind a panel fails, the panel says it did not complete rather than showing an empty result.

title: Briefing view
summary: Turn reviewed evidence into a timed public-comment outline.

paragraphs: Briefing is local. Your outline is saved in this app on this Mac and nothing is submitted anywhere. If saving fails, the view tells you to download your notes before leaving.

sections.heading: Steps
items: Frame the presentation: title, meeting date and body, speaking time, opening, and the requested action.
Interrogate the record: prompts that open Evidence search.

Build the evidence board: the first time it opens it drafts a starting set from the top findings. You review and promote. Each card moves from Saved lead to Source reviewed to Presentation ready and carries a context or limitation note.
Check the promotion standard: at least one traceable item, one that reaches the underlying document, one marked ready, a limitation recorded, and a measurable requested action.
Export outline downloads a Markdown file with evidence locators, source URLs, file hashes when available, and operator-assessment labels.

title: Story desk view
summary: Findings ranked by observable factors, and the full findings inbox, with the fact behind each factor shown.

paragraphs: Story desk orders undismissed findings by what the records show: money at stake, how many documents, requests and agencies repeat the pattern, a record contradicting a statement, a counted violation, evidence strength and freshness.

sections.heading: What the score is
paragraphs: The attention score ranks where to look first. It is not a measure of newsworthiness and not a claim about any record. Each lead is labelled either counted violation or pattern signal; only a counted violation may use the word.

sections.heading: Actions
items: The headline opens the finding's evidence chain in the inspector: the claim, its basis, each cited passage, the file that holds it and that file's last provenance check.
Inspect opens the evidence view filtered to the lead's agency.
Add to briefing copies the finding's evidence into the briefing; a lead with no request anchor cannot be added.
Refresh re-ranks from the current findings.
All findings switches to the full findings inbox. The window control limits ranked leads to those first seen in that window.

title: Compare agencies view
summary: Every agency with an analytics profile, ranked across portals on measured closure latencies and counts.

paragraphs: Compare agencies lists each agency profile the analytics pass produced, across every portal, and sorts it on one measured column: average closure days, closure sample size, performance z-score, statutory violation count and rate, suspiciously fast closures, requests processed, or documents released. Click a column heading to sort by it; click again to reverse. The portal filter narrows the table to one portal.

sections.heading: What a rank is
paragraphs: A rank is a position on a measured latency or count. It is not a compliance judgment. Only the statutory violation column is a counted violation; every other column is a measurement. An agency whose z-score is at or above 2.0 is marked slower than peers, which says nothing about whether any statute was met. An agency with fewer than five measured closures is marked small sample because one closure moves its average.

An agency that has closed nothing measurable shows no measurable closure instead of a number. Zero days would be the fastest possible answer, and an agency that has never closed a request is not fast.

sections.heading: When the table is empty
paragraphs: Profiles are computed when a source finishes syncing or an auxiliary event import completes. If none exist yet, sync a source from the San Diego desk or the sidebar and the table fills when analytics finishes.

title: Meetings view
summary: A calendar of council, board and commission meetings found in collected agendas, minutes and videos, with cited items to watch and public-comment drafts.

paragraphs: Meetings come only from documents already collected. A meeting's body and date are read from the heading of its own agenda, minutes or video. When no heading carries a single weekday and full date, the meeting is listed under Date not recorded rather than placed on a guessed day. A meeting on today's date counts as upcoming.
Agenda, minutes and video are grouped as one meeting only when they share the publisher's meeting identifier, or name the same body and the same heading date.

sections.heading: Items to watch
items: Investigation topic: the item names a term of one of the research topics. Basis: Stated.
Watched agency or party: the item names an agency from your monitoring coverage expectations, or a responsible party from a casework commitment. Basis: Stated.

Stored finding subject: the item names the agency a stored finding is about. Basis: Counted for a counted legal comparison, Pattern for a pattern observation. The mention does not extend the finding to the item.
Evidence gap: the item names the kind of record an open gap needs. A gap is an untested route, never a finding.
Stated figure: the item states a budget or spending figure that the imported tables can be compared with. Counted when compared, Stated when the comparison could not be made.

sections.heading: Public-comment drafts
paragraphs: Each item to watch carries an editable draft that quotes only the cited agenda text, names its basis, and gives the comment deadline and instructions only when an agenda records them; otherwise it says not recorded. Stored findings are referenced by id, not quoted. The draft does not characterize anyone's motives or the lawfulness of any action, and nothing is sent.
